data.name: Nikolos
data.gender_notes: Nikolos is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek 'nikos' meaning victory, and 'laos' meaning people. In Christian tradition, Nikolos is associated with Saint Nicholas, the fourth-century bishop known for his generosity and miracles. The name Nikolos carries the meaning “Victory of the people” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Nikolos usually hope their child will grow to embody victory of the people and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the victory of faith and love over adversity.
data.etymology: Nikolos belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Victory of the people.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nikolos total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.
data.cultural_impact: The name Nikolos holds an enduring place in Western culture, particularly in the tale of Saint Nicholas, whose legend has evolved into the image of Santa Claus. This figure, known for his gift-giving and secret acts of kindness, embodies the spirit of generosity, compassion, and joy during the Christmas season.
data.spiritual_significance: In its most profound sense, the name Nikolos serves as a reminder of the power of love and selflessness, inspired by the life and deeds of Saint Nicholas. By carrying this name, one acknowledges the spiritual gift of victory over challenges and hardships, and the call to extend kindness and generosity to others.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Nikolos carries profound spiritual symbolism as it is rooted in Biblical tradition. As a name associated with Saint Saint Nicholas of Myra, it represents holiness, devotion, and Christian virtue.
